note: For most of the industry's history the United States set no limit on what a drug could cost. The Inflation Reduction Act changed that for Medicare, and the first negotiated prices took effect on 1 January 2026 — the figures below are what actually happened, not a forecast.

rules.before: No cap. A manufacturer set the launch price and raised it at will
rules.now: Medicare negotiates a Maximum Fair Price for a growing list of drugs, rebates back price rises above inflation, and caps Part D out-of-pocket costs at $2,000 a year
rules.catch: Only Medicare, only selected drugs, and only after 9 years on the market for a small molecule or 13 for a biologic

rules.now: A company sets its own price for the first year. A benefit assessment then decides how much better the drug is than what exists, and the price is negotiated from there
rules.catch: Fast access, with the reckoning deferred rather than avoided

rules.now: NICE compares the health gained against the cost and declines to buy above a threshold per quality-adjusted life year
rules.catch: A drug that fails the threshold may simply not be sold

profitCap: There is no cap on profit anywhere in this list. Every mechanism above works on price or on volume, not on margin — no government tells a drug company what it may earn.
sources: Negotiated prices and discounts: CMS and HHS/ASPE, Medicare Drug Price Negotiation Program. Prices are per 30-day equivalent supply and took effect 1 January 2026.

Savings and reach: CMS projections of about $6B net in the first year and $1.5B in out-of-pocket savings across 8.8 million beneficiaries; the ten drugs previously accounted for roughly $50.5B of annual Medicare spending.
Eligibility timing: a small molecule becomes eligible for selection 7 years after approval with a negotiated price from year 9; a biologic 11 and 13 years respectively.
Germany: the 2011 Pharmaceutical Market Restructuring Act (AMNOG) — free pricing in year one, then benefit assessment and negotiation. England: NICE cost-effectiveness thresholds per QALY.
